title: Bug: test_bgp_update_timer.py fails in L3 scenario due to ExaBGP neighbors flapping
author: Stas0k
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

The tests `test_bgp_update_timer_single_route`, `test_bgp_update_timer_session_down` consistently fail in **L3 scenario** (`m0_l3_scenario`) but pass in **VLAN scenario** (`m0_vlan_scenario`).

**Test Setup - L3 scenario**:

```
                    ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                    │              DUT                    │
                    │         (BGP AS 65100)              │
                    │                                     │
                    │   20.0.0.0 ◄────────► 20.0.0.2      │
                    └───────┬─────────────────────┬───────┘
                            │                     │
                      IN    │                     │    OUT
                      ▲     │                     │     ▼
              ┌─────────────┴──┐               ┌──┴─────────────┐
              │  n0 (ExaBGP)   │               │  n1 (ExaBGP)   │
              │   20.0.0.1     │               │   20.0.0.3     │
              │  (AS 61000)    │               │  (AS 61001)    │
              └────────────────┘               └────────────────┘
```

**Test Setup - VLAN scenario**:

```
                    ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                    │              DUT                    │
                    │         (BGP AS 65100)              │
                    │                                     │
                    │             192.168.0.1             │
                    └───────┬─────────────────────┬───────┘
                            │                     │
                     IN     │                     │    OUT
                      ▲     │                     │     ▼
              ┌─────────────┴──┐               ┌──┴─────────────┐
              │  n0 (ExaBGP)   │               │  n1 (ExaBGP)   │
              │  192.168.0.2   │               │  192.168.0.3   │
              │  (AS 61000)    │               │  (AS 61001)    │
              └────────────────┘               └────────────────┘
```


**Root Cause:**
- In L3 scenario, the test configures secondary IPv4 address (20.0.0.0 and 20.0.0.2) on routed interfaces connected to existing ARISTA BGP neighbors.
- In L3 scenario, test creates ExaBGP neighbors (e.g., 20.0.0.1 and 20.0.0.3) and assigns them to the `PEER_V4` peer-group

IP interface config:
```bash

Ethernet47                10.0.0.66/31         up/up         ARISTA02MX      10.0.0.67
Loopback0                 10.1.0.32/32         up/up         N/A             N/A
PortChannel101            10.0.0.56/31         up/up         ARISTA01M1      10.0.0.57
                          20.0.0.2/31                        pseudoswitch1   20.0.0.3
PortChannel103            10.0.0.58/31         up/up         ARISTA02M1      10.0.0.59
PortChannel105            10.0.0.60/31         up/up         ARISTA03M1      10.0.0.61
PortChannel106            10.0.0.62/31         up/up         ARISTA04M1      10.0.0.63
                          20.0.0.0/31                        pseudoswitch0   20.0.0.1
Vlan1000                  192.168.0.1/24       up/up         N/A             N/A
docker0                   240.127.1.1/24       up/down       N/A             N/A
eth0                      10.2.139.51/24       up/up         N/A             N/A
lo                        127.0.0.1/16         up/up         N/A             N/A
admin@DUT-1:~$
```

BGP peer groups:
```bash
show runningconfig bgp
...
 neighbor 20.0.0.1 remote-as 61000
 neighbor 20.0.0.1 peer-group PEER_V4
 neighbor 20.0.0.1 description pseudoswitch0
 neighbor 20.0.0.1 timers 3 10
 neighbor 20.0.0.1 timers connect 10
 neighbor 20.0.0.3 remote-as 61001
 neighbor 20.0.0.3 peer-group PEER_V4
 neighbor 20.0.0.3 description pseudoswitch1
 neighbor 20.0.0.3 timers 3 10
 neighbor 20.0.0.3 timers connect 10
```

The `PEER_V4` peer-group has a route-map `TO_BGP_PEER_V4 out` that **permits all routes**:
```bash
route-map TO_BGP_PEER_V4 permit 100
  call CHECK_IDF_ISOLATION
exit
 ...

  neighbor PEER_V4 route-map TO_BGP_PEER_V4 out
```

DUT sends **thousands of routes** learned from ARISTA neighbors to ExaBGP neghbors. ExaBGP cannot handle this flood, causing:
- BGP sessions to flap continuously
- `State/PfxRcd` always flaps between `Idle`, `Active`, or `0` (non-stable neighbors)
- Test assertions to fail because expected BGP UPDATE packets are not captured

**Why L3 scenario fails but VLAN scenario passes:**
In VLAN scenario, ExaBGP neighbors are configured within the `192.168.0.0/24` range on Vlan1000:

```bash
admin@DUT-1:~$ show ip int
Interface       Master    IPv4 address/mask    Admin/Oper    BGP Neighbor    Neighbor IP
--------------  --------  -------------------  ------------  --------------  -------------
Ethernet46                10.0.0.64/31         up/up         ARISTA01MX      10.0.0.65
Ethernet47                10.0.0.66/31         up/up         ARISTA02MX      10.0.0.67
Loopback0                 10.1.0.32/32         up/up         N/A             N/A
PortChannel101            10.0.0.56/31         up/up         ARISTA01M1      10.0.0.57
PortChannel103            10.0.0.58/31         up/up         ARISTA02M1      10.0.0.59
PortChannel105            10.0.0.60/31         up/up         ARISTA03M1      10.0.0.61
PortChannel106            10.0.0.62/31         up/up         ARISTA04M1      10.0.0.63
Vlan1000                  192.168.0.1/24       up/up         pseudoswitch0   192.168.0.2
docker0                   240.127.1.1/24       up/down       N/A             N/A
eth0                      10.2.139.51/24       up/up         N/A             N/A
lo                        127.0.0.1/16         up/up         N/A             N/A
admin@DUT-1:~$
```

**PCAP Evidence:**
- In L3 scenario - captured packets show DUT (20.0.0.0) sending large BGP UPDATE messages with thousands of NLRI entries to ExaBGP (20.0.0.1), causing session instability.
- In VLAN scenario - only desired routes 10.10.100.X/27 announce and withdraw

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up a testbed with M0 topology 
2. Run test cases:
	- `bgp/test_bgp_update_timer.py::test_bgp_update_timer_single_route[DUT-1-m0_l3_scenario]`
	- `bgp/test_bgp_update_timer.py::test_bgp_update_timer_session_down[DUT-1-m0_l3_scenario]`
3. Observe test failure with errors like:
```bash
==========================================================
FAILED bgp/test_bgp_update_timer.py::test_bgp_update_timer_single_route[DUT-1-m0_l3_scenario] - Failed: no bgp update withdraw route {'prefix': '10.10.100.64/27', 'nexthop': '20.0.0.1'} from 20.0.0.1 to 20.0.0.0
========================================================================================================================== 1 failed, 1 warning in 870.07s (0:14:30) ==========================================================================================================================
DEBUG:tests.conftest:[log_custom_msg] item: <Function test_bgp_update_timer_single_route[DUT-1-m0_l3_scenario]>
```
```bash
FAILED bgp/test_bgp_update_timer.py::test_bgp_update_timer_single_route[DUT-1-m0_l3_scenario] - Failed: no bgp update announce route {'prefix': '10.10.100.0/27', 'nexthop': '20.0.0.1'} from 20.0.0.2 to 20.0.0.3
========================================================================================================================== 1 failed, 1 warning in 656.74s (0:10:56) ==========================================================================================================================
DEBUG:tests.conftest:[log_custom_msg] item: <Function test_bgp_update_timer_single_route[DUT-1-m0_l3_scenario]>
```

4. During test execution, check BGP neighbor status on DUT. ExaBGP neighbors (20.0.0.1, 20.0.0.3) will show flapping state.

5. Run the same tests with VLAN scenario - test pass:
- `bgp/test_bgp_update_timer.py::test_bgp_update_timer_single_route[DUT-1-m0_vlan_scenario]`
- `bgp/test_bgp_update_timer.py::test_bgp_update_timer_session_down[DUT-1-m0_vlan_scenario]`

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

**Actual Behavior:**
- DUT floods ExaBGP with thousands of routes from ARISTA neighbors
- In L3 scenario (shared PortChannel interface), ExaBGP sessions flap
- Test fails because expected BGP UPDATE packets are not captured reliably

**Expected Behavior:**
- ExaBGP neighbors should have a route-map that only permits test routes (10.10.100.0/24 range) outbound
- BGP sessions should remain stable throughout the test
- Test should pass consistently in both L3 and VLAN scenarios

**Workaround:**

Manually applying a restrictive route-map on DUT to ExaBGP neighbors after n0, n1 session establishment - fixes the issue:

```bash
vtysh -c "configure terminal" \
      -c "ip prefix-list PL_TEST_ROUTES seq 10 permit 10.10.100.0/24 le 32" \
      -c "route-map RM_TEST_ONLY permit 10" \
      -c "match ip address prefix-list PL_TEST_ROUTES" \
      -c "route-map RM_TEST_ONLY deny 20" \
      -c "router bgp 65100" \
      -c "address-family ipv4 unicast" \
      -c "neighbor 20.0.0.1 route-map RM_TEST_ONLY out" \
      -c "neighbor 20.0.0.3 route-map RM_TEST_ONLY out"

vtysh -c "clear ip bgp 20.0.0.1 soft out"
vtysh -c "clear ip bgp 20.0.0.3 soft out"
```

After applying this, BGP sessions stabilize and the test passes.
```bash
========================================================================================================================= 1 passed, 1 warning in 2637.83s (0:43:57) ==========================================================================================================================
DEBUG:tests.conftest:[log_custom_msg] item: <Function test_bgp_update_timer_single_route[DUT-1-m0_l3_scenario]>
```

comments.author: bpar9
comments.body: @Stas0k instead of adding the restrictive route-map to match/limit the routes in L3 scenario, can we actually check why BGP sessions are flapping when large number of routes sent? is this expected or a test restriction?

comments.author: Stas0k
comments.body:
Hi @bpar9:

Q: Can we actually check why BGP sessions are flapping when large number of routes sent? is this expected or a test restriction?
A:
- I would divide it into 2 questions:
1) Why there is an ExaBGP neighbor failure when sending large num. of routes ?  (Not expected)
2) Is the test correct? Was it expected to send large amount of routes coming from Arista or not (since these are "background" routes - they are not verified in the test, and VLAN scenario doesn't do it) ?

**Observation**:  
- The flapping observed only with ExaBGP peers (not expected). For example BGP session is stable with ~1.5K routes with DUT connected to Arista cEOS as a BGP peer. 
- The restrictive route-map was added only for debug purposes to eliminate the problem. 
- Test behavior question: Don't know what the purpose of the test with L3 scenario - but I see that goal is to verify only the announce and withdraw packets from/to test neighbors (ExaBGP neighbors created by the test) - n0 (pseudoswitch0) and n1 (pseudoswitch1). 
Test fails due to unstable ExaBGP neighbors as a result of big amount of advertised routes that come from Arista (M0 topology setup, not the test itself). Is there a need for extra "background" routes arrived from Arista (M0 topology env)? Need to understand if this was the purpose of the test or mistake.

**Conclusion**:
From my observation the issue comes from unstable ExaBGP peers. There can be a performance issue in ExaBGP that can't handle big amount of routes or BGP misconfiguration (keepalive, hold-down timers).  Did someone observe similar issue in M0 topology? Or tried to announce big amount of routes to ExaBGP neighbor and observed neighbor failure?

linkedPullRequests.title: [bgp] Fix BGP update timer test ExaBGP session flapping in L3 scenario (#22391)
linkedPullRequests.author: yxieca
linkedPullRequests.body:
### Description of PR
Fixes https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/issues/22391

#### Summary
When ExaBGP test neighbors are configured on routed interfaces that already have real BGP peers (e.g. M0 L3 scenario with `PEER_V4` peer-group), the DUT floods ExaBGP with thousands of learned routes from the full routing table. ExaBGP cannot handle this volume, causing continuous session flapping and consistent test failures for:
- `test_bgp_update_timer_single_route[*-m0_l3_scenario]`
- `test_bgp_update_timer_session_down[*-m0_l3_scenario]`

#### Root Cause
In L3 scenario, ExaBGP neighbors get added to the `PEER_V4` peer-group which has a permissive outbound route-map (`TO_BGP_PEER_V4`) that advertises all routes. The DUT sends thousands of NLRI entries to ExaBGP, overwhelming it and causing BGP session instability.

#### Fix
After ExaBGP sessions are established, apply a restrictive outbound route-map that only permits test route prefixes (`10.10.100.0/24` for IPv4, `fc00:1x::/48` for IPv6). The route-map is cleaned up in the test teardown.

This approach was validated by the issue reporter as a working workaround.

### Type of change
- [x] Bug fix

### Back port request
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202405

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
The `test_bgp_update_timer` tests consistently fail on M0 L3 topologies because ExaBGP sessions flap under route flooding.

#### How did you do it?
Added helper functions `_apply_outbound_route_filter()` and `_remove_outbound_route_filter()` that:
1. Create a prefix-list matching only test route prefixes
2. Create a route-map that permits only those prefixes
3. Apply the route-map as outbound policy to ExaBGP neighbors
4. Soft-reset BGP so the filter takes effect immediately
5. Clean up everything in the finally block

#### How did you verify/test it?
- Code passes flake8 with max-line-length=120
- Fix matches the exact workaround validated by the issue reporter
- The route-map logic is standard FRR configuration used elsewhere in sonic-mgmt
